keyVerseText: He was twenty and five years old when he began to reign, and reigned twenty and nine years in Jerusalem. And his mother's name was Jehoaddan of Jerusalem.
rootMeaning: The name יְהוֹעַדִּין (Jehoaddan) derives from the Hebrew components יְהֹוָה (Jehovah), the proper name of God meaning 'the existing One,' and עָדַן, meaning 'pleased' or 'delighted.' Thus, the literal meaning of the name is 'Jehovah delights' or 'Jehovah is pleased.' This etymology emphasizes a personal and relational aspect of God as one who finds delight or pleasure, which adds depth beyond the common English gloss by highlighting God's favorable disposition.
usageInScripture: The word יְהוֹעַדִּין appears twice in Scripture, both times as a proper name referring to the same individual: the mother of King Amaziah of Judah. It is consistently translated as 'Jehoaddan,' indicating a specific person rather than a common noun or title. This consistency in translation underscores the name's role in identifying a historical figure within the royal lineage of Judah.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding the meaning of Jehoaddan as 'Jehovah delights' enriches our appreciation of God's character as one who delights in His people and in His plans. It reminds believers that even in the naming of individuals within Scripture, the presence and pleasure of God are central. This name, borne by the mother of a king, reflects the intertwining of divine favor with the covenant community's leadership, pointing ultimately to God's sovereign delight in the lineage through which the Messiah would come. Such a name encourages faith in a God who is not distant but actively pleased with His creation and His redemptive purposes.
keyVerseReflection: In 2 Kings 14:2, the text states, 'And his mother's name was Jehoaddan of Jerusalem,' linking Amaziah's identity to his mother, whose name means 'Jehovah delights.' This detail highlights the significance of divine favor surrounding Amaziah's lineage. The presence of this name in the verse subtly affirms that Amaziah's reign is under the auspices of a God who delights, suggesting that God's pleasure and blessing are foundational to the king's legitimacy and the unfolding history of Judah.
